constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects: Quarry may enforce only what the broker-signed grant contains and must never read Control Plane rules (no cross-plane DB), so rules are compiled into the grant at issue time with an embedded policy version. Plane ownership: durable rules belong in Control Plane (user-core user settings and an org policy object); the broker is a decision point and today is in-memory. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so rules are per user or org, never per Space. ZDR must propagate: persistent always-allow scopes store host names, so limit ZDR orgs to turn scope (INF). Policy evaluation stays fail-closed and every deny and approve is audited. Open owner decision OD13 (fence of start host plus at most 8 user-listed domains, broker as authority) should be settled before the pattern language is designed.
approachAdjustment: Split into three deliverables and fix two placement errors. (1) Typed denials first (S-M, Ingestion plus execution-core): add a browser DenialReason enum with decision_source and make the Quarry error code match the HTTP status (status_err currently emits BAD_REQUEST for 403s), modelled on CrawlDenialReason. (2) Per-origin consent (L): the item's 'broker issues a child grant with the new origin' does not work with current semantics, because child grants allow exactly one of three sensitive actions and validate_run_grant demands run domains equal the parent grant at every step; add a new parent-bound origin-extension grant kind that Quarry validates, then widen the live policy through configure_egress_policy, or end and resume with a new grant (resume is blocked by the same equality check). Persist conversation and always decisions in Control Plane user settings, not the broker. (3) Org origin policy and Settings > Browser hub (L): Control Plane owns the versioned policy and the broker intersects it at grant issue. Keep the wildcard pattern language out until grant.go isCanonicalDomain and BrowserEgressPolicy::canonical_broker_domains change together. Fold the saved-approval part of F-t2-073 into this item.
effortNote: As a single item it spans Model, Ingestion, Control and Frontend planes and needs a new Quarry grant kind plus a durable rule store; split it as S-M (typed denials) + L (per-origin consent) + L (org policy and hub).
verdictReason: The gap is real (no per-origin consent, typed denials, run modes or policy hub), but the child-grant mechanism and the broker as persistence layer conflict with the code (single-action child grants, run domains fixed to the grant, in-memory store), so the bundle should be split and sequenced with typed denials first.

(3) Product usage events should not add a SPA analytics client: emit enum-only counters server-side from the gateway or execution-core into the existing usage v2 subject, suppressed for ZDR orgs. Quarry must first publish decision audit (F-t2-036) before an export is meaningful for browser actions.
